title: CPR (Heart Attack & Arrest)
warningBanner: If person is unresponsive and not breathing normally, start CPR immediately.

steps.title: Check Response & Breathing
steps.body: Tap shoulders firmly and shout: 'Are you OK?'. Check chest movement for 5 seconds.

steps.title: Call 108 Ambulance
steps.body: Shout for help and dial 108 immediately. Put phone on speaker.

steps.title: Place Hands in Center of Chest
steps.body: Place heel of one hand in center of chest between nipples. Interlock other hand on top.

steps.title: Push Hard & Fast (100–120 bpm)
steps.body: Push down 5–6 cm deep at 100 to 120 beats per minute. Allow chest to fully recoil.

steps.title: Give 2 Rescue Breaths (If Trained)
steps.body: Tilt head back, pinch nose, and blow 2 breaths. Continue 30 compressions and 2 breaths until help arrives.

dos: Push hard and fast in center of chest (100–120 bpm)
Let chest come all the way up between compressions
Call 108 and keep phone on speaker mode
Switch with another person every 2 minutes if tired
donts: Do NOT delay compressions to check pulse
Do NOT bend your elbows while pushing
Do NOT stop compressions until ambulance arrives or person wakes up

title: Unconsciousness / Fainting

steps.title: Check Response & Breathing
steps.body: Tap shoulders firmly and ask loudly: 'Are you OK?'. Look at chest for 5-10 seconds.

steps.title: Open Airway & Turn on Side
steps.body: Gently tilt head back and lift chin. Turn onto side (recovery position) if breathing.

steps.title: Call 108 Ambulance
steps.body: Dial 108 immediately. If NOT breathing normally, begin CPR immediately.

dos: Check responsiveness and normal breathing
Place in side recovery position if breathing
Loosen tight clothing and ensure fresh air
Call 108 ambulance
donts: Do NOT give anything to eat or drink
Do NOT shake a baby or child violently
Do NOT place pillow under head if not breathing

title: Choking
warningBanner: If person cannot breathe, speak, or cough, act immediately.

steps.title: Encourage Forceful Coughing
steps.body: If the person can cough or speak, encourage them to keep coughing hard.

steps.title: Deliver 5 Firm Back Blows
steps.body: Lean person forward and deliver 5 firm blows between shoulder blades with heel of hand.

steps.title: Perform 5 Abdominal Thrusts (Heimlich)
steps.body: Stand behind person, place fist above belly button, and pull sharply inward and upward 5 times.

steps.title: Repeat Back Blows & Thrusts
steps.body: Alternate 5 back blows and 5 thrusts until the object clears. If unconscious, lower to ground and start CPR.

dos: Encourage strong coughing if airway is partially open
Alternate 5 back blows with 5 abdominal thrusts
Call 108 if blockage does not clear immediately
donts: Do NOT give abdominal thrusts to infants (use back slaps & chest thrusts)
Do NOT perform blind finger sweeps in the mouth
Do NOT slap on the back if person is standing upright

title: Severe Bleeding
warningBanner: Direct continuous pressure is the most effective way to stop severe bleeding.

steps.title: Apply Direct Firm Pressure
steps.body: Press firmly on the bleeding wound using a clean cloth, sterile gauze, or bare hands.

steps.title: Elevate Wounded Limb
steps.body: Raise the bleeding arm or leg above heart level while continuing firm pressure.

steps.title: Maintain Continuous Pressure for 10 Min
steps.body: Keep pressing without lifting cloth. If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top.

steps.title: Bandage Firmly & Call 108
steps.body: Wrap a tight bandage over the dressing. Call 108 or rush to PHC. Keep person warm.

dos: Press continuously with clean cloth for 10 minutes
Elevate the injured limb above heart level
Add more cloth layers if blood soaks through
Keep the person warm with a blanket
donts: Do NOT remove embedded objects (e.g. knives, glass, metal)
Do NOT wash deep, severely bleeding wounds with water
Do NOT remove the first soaked cloth layer

title: Burns & Scalds
warningBanner: Use cool running tap water only. Never apply toothpaste, butter, or oil.

steps.title: Cool with Running Tap Water
steps.body: Hold burn under cool running tap water for 15–20 minutes immediately. Never use ice.

steps.title: Remove Rings & Constrictive Items
steps.body: Take off rings, bangles, and tight clothes before swelling. Do not peel stuck clothes.

steps.title: Cover Loosely with Clean Cloth
steps.body: Cover loosely with clean plastic cling wrap or sterile non-stick cloth to prevent infection.

steps.title: Seek Medical Care
steps.body: Visit PHC or call 108 if burn is larger than palm, on face/hands, or if victim is a child.

dos: Cool under running water for 15 to 20 minutes
Cover loosely with clean plastic wrap or sterile cloth
Give clean water sips to prevent dehydration
donts: Do NOT apply toothpaste, butter, mud, turmeric, or oil
Do NOT apply ice directly on burned skin
Do NOT burst blisters or peel stuck clothing

title: Fracture & Immobilization
warningBanner: Do not try to realign or push back a broken bone.

steps.title: Support in Current Position
steps.body: Do not move or straighten the broken bone. Keep it supported in the exact position found.

steps.title: Apply Temporary Rigid Splint
steps.body: Use a rolled towel, cardboard, or wooden stick to immobilize joints above and below fracture.

steps.title: Apply Ice Pack Wrapped in Cloth
steps.body: Place an ice pack wrapped in a towel on the area for 15 minutes to control swelling.

steps.title: Carefully Transport to Hospital
steps.body: Transport to CHC or District Hospital for X-ray and casting. Do not put weight on limb.

dos: Immobilize joint above and below fracture site
Support with padded splint, cardboard, or sling
Apply ice pack wrapped in a cloth
donts: Do NOT attempt to straighten or push back a broken bone
Do NOT massage or apply pressure to injured bone
Do NOT allow patient to walk on broken leg

title: Snake Bite
warningBanner: Do NOT suck venom, cut the skin, or apply tight tourniquets.

steps.title: Stay Calm & Keep Person Still
steps.body: Make victim lie down completely still. Movement spreads venom faster through the body.

steps.title: Remove Rings & Tight Items
steps.body: Quickly remove rings, bangles, anklets, and tight clothing before swelling starts.

steps.title: Immobilize Limb Below Heart
steps.body: Keep bitten limb lower than heart level. Secure with a loose splint or sling.

steps.title: Cover Loosely with Clean Cloth
steps.body: Wipe bite area with clean water and cover loosely with a clean, dry cloth.

steps.title: Call 108 & Rush for ASV
steps.body: Call 108 ambulance immediately or rush to PHC/hospital with Anti-Snake Venom (ASV).

dos: Keep victim calm and completely motionless
Remove jewelry and tight clothing near bite
Immobilize the bitten limb with a splint
Rush to hospital with Anti-Snake Venom (ASV)
donts: Do NOT cut, slash, or burn the bite area
Do NOT suck venom with mouth or suction devices
Do NOT tie tight tourniquets or apply ice/chemicals
Do NOT give tea, coffee, alcohol, or herbal medicines

title: Electric Shock
warningBanner: Never touch victim directly while they are still in contact with electrical source.

steps.title: Turn Off Power Source
steps.body: Immediately switch off the main circuit breaker or unplug the wire. Do not touch victim.

steps.title: Separate with Non-Conductive Item
steps.body: If power cannot be cut, push wire away using dry wooden stick, broom, plastic, or rubber.

steps.title: Check Breathing & Airway
steps.body: Once safe, check response and breathing. If not breathing, start CPR compressions immediately.

steps.title: Call 108 & Recovery Position
steps.body: Call 108 ambulance. If breathing, place in side recovery position and cover burn spots.

dos: Turn off the main electrical power switch first
Use dry wood, plastic, or rubber to push wire away
Check breathing and start CPR if unresponsive
Call 108 ambulance immediately
donts: Do NOT touch the victim with bare hands while connected to power
Do NOT use wet objects or metal to separate the wire
Do NOT move victim if neck or spinal injury is suspected

title: Heat Stroke & Dehydration
warningBanner: High body temperature (>40°C) with confusion is a critical medical emergency.

steps.title: Move to Cool Shade Immediately
steps.body: Move person out of the hot sun into shade or an airy room. Loosen heavy clothing.

steps.title: Rapidly Cool the Skin
steps.body: Sponge cool water all over skin. Place wet cloths or ice packs on neck, armpits, and groin.

steps.title: Fan Continuously
steps.body: Fan the person vigorously with electric or hand fan to speed up body cooling.

steps.title: Give ORS if Conscious & Call 108
steps.body: If awake, give small sips of ORS or water. If confused or vomiting, call 108 right away.

dos: Move to shaded, airy area immediately
Apply cool wet cloths to neck, armpits, and groin
Fan continuously and give ORS if conscious
Call 108 if person is confused or unresponsive
donts: Do NOT give fluids to an unconscious or vomiting person
Do NOT give paracetamol or aspirin for heat stroke
Do NOT use freezing ice baths (causes shivering)

title: Chest Pain / Heart Attack
warningBanner: Chest pain radiating to arm, jaw, or neck requires immediate emergency care.

steps.title: Make Person Sit Upright
steps.body: Help person sit comfortably leaning against wall. Loosen tight collar and waist.

steps.title: Call 108 Immediately
steps.body: Dial 108 right away. Tell operator you suspect a heart attack.

steps.title: Aspirin if Prescribed
steps.body: If person has prescribed heart medicine (Sorbitrate / Aspirin) and no allergy, have them chew it.

steps.title: Monitor Breathing & Prepare CPR
steps.body: Stay calm beside victim. If they lose consciousness and stop breathing, begin CPR.

dos: Sit person upright with knees bent (W position)
Call 108 ambulance immediately
Keep surrounding quiet and well-ventilated
donts: Do NOT allow person to walk or exert themselves
Do NOT give heavy food or water
Do NOT leave person unattended

title: Pesticide & Poisoning
warningBanner: Do NOT induce vomiting unless specifically advised by a doctor.

steps.title: Move to Fresh Open Air
steps.body: Move victim away from pesticide spray, toxic fumes, or poison area into fresh air.

steps.title: Strip Clothes & Wash Skin
steps.body: Remove contaminated clothes and wash skin with soap and plenty of running water.

steps.title: Preserve Container / Chemical Label
steps.body: Keep the pesticide bottle or chemical packet to show doctors at the hospital.

steps.title: Call 108 & Transport Immediately
steps.body: Call 108 ambulance. Report chemical name and rush to nearest equipped hospital.

dos: Move to fresh air immediately
Wash exposed skin with soap and plenty of water
Bring chemical container or label to hospital
donts: Do NOT induce vomiting (can burn food pipe)
Do NOT give raw eggs, kerosene, or home remedies
Do NOT give fluids if person is drowsy

title: High Fever & Fits
warningBanner: Watch for seizures (fits) in children with very high fever.

steps.title: Tepid Water Sponging
steps.body: Wipe forehead, neck, chest, and arms with cloth dipped in lukewarm (not ice) water.

steps.title: Offer Small Sips of Fluids
steps.body: Offer clean water, coconut water, rice water, dal water, or ORS in small sips.

steps.title: If Seizure / Fit Occurs
steps.body: Turn person on their side. Clear nearby sharp objects. Do not hold them down.

steps.title: Visit PHC for Evaluation
steps.body: Visit PHC to test for infection. Call 108 if fever exceeds 104°F or fits last >5 minutes.

dos: Sponge with lukewarm tap water
Encourage plenty of fluids and rest
Turn on side in recovery position if seizure occurs
donts: Do NOT use ice or alcohol for sponging
Do NOT put onion, keys, or spoons in mouth during fits
Do NOT bundle up in heavy blankets
